wiki-iran.standing: The daily count of people opening the English Wikipedia article on Iran. It rises when the country enters a story large enough to send readers looking for background, so the line tracks public attention rather than events themselves.
wiki-iran.recent: US forces struck three Iranian crude tankers and Iran said it hit six in reply, leaving the Strait of Hormuz in a stalemate that killed two Filipino sailors aboard the tanker Sidr. Iran's security chief vowed a prohibited zone in the strait, and Energy Secretary Chris Wright said there may be no nuclear agreement — the aim the war was declared to serve.

brent.standing: The light, sweet North Sea grade that prices roughly two-thirds of internationally traded crude, from West African cargoes to Asian refinery contracts. Most oil-importing economies pay a bill indexed to it.
brent.recent: US forces struck three Iranian crude tankers and Iran said it hit six in reply, leaving the Strait of Hormuz — the route for a fifth of seaborne crude — a corridor tankers now turn back from and Tehran has threatened to declare a prohibited zone. OPEC+ left quotas unchanged rather than cover the outage, and US pump prices reached $4.03 a gallon.

wti.standing: The US light sweet benchmark, priced for delivery at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the grade American refiners and shale producers settle against. It is landlocked, so it usually trades below seaborne grades, and US pump prices follow it.
wti.recent: Fighting in the Gulf reached the tankers themselves: the US struck three Iranian crude carriers and Iran says it hit six in reply, three ships turned back at Hormuz without a shot fired, and Iran's security chief vowed to declare a prohibited zone in the strait. OPEC+ met in Riyadh and left quotas unchanged, declining to cover any outage. India's import basket cleared $101.07.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for natural gas delivered to a pipeline junction in Erath, Louisiana, quoted per million British thermal units. American power generation, heating and LNG export contracts are priced off it, and it sets the floor cost of US cargoes sold abroad.
natgas-hh.recent: The American price detached from the rest of the world: European gas cleared €75 per megawatt-hour with EU storage near 64%, and the competition for spot LNG pushed Delhi to raise compressed natural gas by ₹3.89 a kilogram and left Pakistan apologising for night-time blackouts after a delayed cargo.

wheat.standing: The IMF's benchmark price for a tonne of milling wheat traded internationally, quoted monthly. It sets what importing governments pay to keep bread subsidies running, so it reaches household budgets in wheat-buying countries long before it reaches farmers.
wheat.recent: Europe's harvest failed under heat and drought, with France's maize crop falling to a four-decade low, and the UN's food price index climbed a third straight month to 133.3 points on cereals and sugar. Forecasters in Geneva put the odds near 100% that El Niño persists to February, and Panama's canal chief is weighing cuts to daily transits that ration bulk grain shipping first.

rice.standing: The world reference price for milled white rice, quoted by the IMF in dollars a tonne. Rice is the staple grain for more people than any other crop, and import bills across Asia and West Africa move with this number.
rice.recent: The UN food agency put its price index up a third straight month, to 133.3 points, on cereals and sugar, with conflict and extreme weather named as the drivers. That basket figure does not break rice out, and nothing else this month accounts for where this contract has gone.

copper.standing: The world price of a tonne of refined copper. It is the metal that carries current, so cables, motors and transformers all price off it, and demand for it follows construction and electrification more closely than almost any other input.
copper.recent: The fortnight's electricity news was about grid security rather than supply: police found 12 explosives along power lines in Saxony days after two substations were hit with homemade devices, and the White House barred foreign grid parts, citing actors "exploiting vulnerabilities." None of that accounts for the price.

us-10y.standing: The yield on the US government's ten-year note, set by what buyers will pay at auction and in the secondary market. It anchors mortgage rates, corporate borrowing costs and the discount rate applied to almost every other asset.
us-10y.recent: Norway's sovereign wealth fund signalled it may shed $80bn of Treasuries, thinning the largest foreign bid outside central banks. An oil shock pushed odds of a Fed hike rather than a cut to two-in-three, and Warsh's Jackson Hole speech left the Fed's independence itself a traded question.

sp500.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of 500 of the largest companies listed on US exchanges, chosen by a committee. It is the benchmark most American pension and retirement money is measured against, so its level sets what ordinary savers think they own.
sp500.recent: Pressure in the window came from the bond market rather than from earnings: global yields hit multi-decade highs on inflation fears in early September, and a solid US jobs report lifted yields and the dollar again, easing stocks. Waller's comments cut briefly the other way, sending the dollar to its weakest since May.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on New York's Nasdaq exchange, weighted by market value. A handful of chipmakers and software firms carry most of that weight, so it moves with them, not with the broad economy.
nasdaq100.recent: Nvidia paid $12.9 billion for Hugging Face, buying the open-source AI hub outright. Huawei launched the Mate XT2 holding 68% of China's foldables, closing the premium tier of that market to Apple days before its September 9 event. Meta settled claims over social media harms to children for $16.68B.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price American drivers pay at the pump for a gallon of regular gasoline, surveyed weekly across the country. It tracks crude oil and refining margins with a lag of a week or two, and it is the most visible price in US household budgets.
us-gas-retail.recent: US pump prices passed $4.03 a gallon, above the 2012 record, as the Iran war fed through crude into refined products; diesel hit $5.85 a gallon the same week, squeezing California trucking and farm freight. The pass-through reached importers too — South African petrol rose R1.34 a litre despite a stronger rand.

natgas-ttf.standing: The Dutch Title Transfer Facility price, the wholesale benchmark for pipeline and imported gas across northwest Europe. It sets what utilities pay for winter supply, and industrial power and fertiliser costs follow it.
natgas-ttf.recent: Europe's benchmark climbed past €75 per megawatt-hour in early September with EU storage sitting near 64%, well short of where refill normally stands before winter, forcing buyers into a spot LNG market they must outbid Asia to reach. That competition carried through to importers: Delhi raised compressed natural gas by ₹3.89 to ₹86.98 a kg.

vix.standing: A gauge of how much price movement traders expect in the S&P 500 over the coming month, derived from what they pay for index options. It rises when hedging gets expensive, which is why it is read as a measure of fear.

fx-pkr.standing: The rupee's exchange rate against the US dollar, set in Pakistan's interbank market. Pakistan imports its fuel and much of its food, and pays external debt in dollars, so the rate feeds straight into domestic prices.
fx-pkr.recent: The fortnight's news from Islamabad was mostly domestic — the PIMS nursery fire that killed 14 infants, a Senate acid-attack bill, a journalist held under cybercrime law — and none of it bears on the exchange rate. The nearest external items were a Mecca joint defence pact meeting with Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, and EU figures putting Pakistan's GSP+ tariff exemptions at €732 million in 2024.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency against the dollar, quoted as naira per dollar. Africa's largest population imports most of its refined fuel and food, so the rate feeds directly into domestic prices, and the oil earnings that back it are dollar-denominated.
fx-ngn.recent: Nigeria's foreign reserves reached a 20-year high, and Moody's credited the austerity behind it. FTSE Russell will reclassify the country from Unclassified to Frontier on September 21, restoring index-tracking inflows, and the Dangote refinery opened to retail buyers at about $4 for ten shares — all of it dollar demand the central bank no longer has to meet alone.

fx-egp.standing: The Egyptian pound's exchange rate against the US dollar. Egypt imports most of its wheat and fuel and services heavy external debt in dollars, so the rate sets the price of bread, energy and repayment alike.
fx-egp.recent: A major Egyptian bank was cut off from the global financial system by the United States in late August, part of a push by Bessent against banks with Iran ties that also reached the UAE. Cairo spent the same fortnight courting alternatives, hosting Xi Jinping on his first state visit in a decade and pressing a Libya settlement.

fx-try.standing: The number of Turkish lira one US dollar buys, quoted by the central bank's counterparties and the price at which Turkey imports its energy. Its slide is the main channel through which Ankara's interest-rate policy reaches household prices.
fx-try.recent: The US Treasury sanctioned Golden Global Bank in Istanbul over Iran-linked dealings, the first designation of a Turkish lender in this round and a reminder to correspondent banks of what Turkish exposure carries. Ankara also summoned Kyiv's ambassador over strikes on Turkish ships, while Erdogan defended an SCO push he calls a "360-degree" foreign policy rather than a turn from NATO.

fx-bdt.standing: The price of one US dollar in Bangladeshi taka, the currency of a country whose foreign earnings rest heavily on garment exports and on remittances sent home by workers in the Gulf. Import bills for fuel and food are settled against it.
fx-bdt.recent: Dhaka confirmed a purchase of Chinese J-10CE fighter jets, a hard-currency defence commitment from a government whose panel had been drafting terms for up to 24 airframes. Bangladesh is also seeking Nepali electricity, a deal India controls the transmission route for, while the garment sector that earns most of the country's dollars faces its own labour costs.

fx-idr.standing: The rupiah's exchange rate against the US dollar, quoted as rupiah per dollar, so a lower number is a stronger rupiah. Indonesia's commodity exports and its imported fuel and food are both priced in dollars, so the rate feeds through to domestic prices quickly.
fx-idr.recent: Jakarta ratified a trade deal with Russia and opened 138 oil and gas exploration blocks to Russian partners, with fertilizer and shipbuilding investment attached. Anak Krakatau's eruption shut Soekarno-Hatta and stranded 166,000 passengers, but the disruption was to aviation rather than to the export earnings the currency runs on.

fx-lbp.standing: The number of Lebanese pounds it takes to buy a US dollar. The central bank abandoned the old peg after the 2019 banking collapse, and the rate it now holds is what wages, imports and savings in the country are measured against.
fx-lbp.recent: Israeli strikes destroyed Ghandour Hospital in Nabatieh al-Fawqa on 6 September, killing seven, part of a campaign the health ministry counts at nearly 9,000 dead in Lebanon since 2023. Israeli forces hold Christian border villages around Ain Ebel, turning back aid convoys, and soil at Ayta ash-Shaab tested at 50 times normal glyphosate levels.

fx-cny.standing: The exchange rate of China's currency against the US dollar, quoted as yuan per dollar. The central bank steers it within a daily band, and it sets the dollar cost of goods from the world's largest manufacturing base.
fx-cny.recent: August customs figures put exports at $401 billion, up 25%, holding through port disruption and a tariff regime built on the premise that American buyers constrain them; the redirection ran to Southeast Asia, Africa, the Gulf and Latin America. Regulators separately handed five state insurers and three banks $53.6 billion in capital.

fx-inr.standing: The price of one US dollar in Indian rupees, quoted as rupees per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker rupee. India buys most of its crude and much of its electronics abroad, and this rate sets what that costs at home.
fx-inr.recent: India's crude import basket passed $101.07 a barrel on Friday, and with roughly 85% of its oil bought abroad, the import bill is settled in dollars. New Delhi also cut last year's economic base by 7% while reporting 7.8% June-quarter growth, a pairing that moved the country to sixth-largest economy when converted at this rate.

fx-brl.standing: The exchange rate of Brazil's currency against the US dollar, quoted as reais per dollar. Brazil is a major exporter of soy, iron ore and oil, and the real tends to track commodity demand and the interest-rate gap with the United States.
fx-brl.recent: Bank Master collapsed in a fraud probe in Brasília, putting the country's bank supervision under scrutiny, and a new poll showed the socialist president's lead evaporating ahead of the election. Separately, the Bank of Korea argued that dollar-pegged stablecoins are pulling local currencies down.

fx-mxn.standing: The exchange rate between Mexico's peso and the US dollar, one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies. Mexico sends most of its exports north, so the rate prices how much of the US economy flows back into Mexican wages.
fx-mxn.recent: Water, not tariffs, is now the binding constraint between the two economies: the 1944 treaty obliges Mexico to deliver a fixed volume from the Rio Grande basin each five-year cycle, and a decade of drought means the water is not there. Because it allocates volumes rather than shares, every shortfall is a breach Washington can attach to trade leverage.

fx-eur.standing: The number of US dollars one euro buys, quoted here inverted as euros per dollar. It is the world's second-most-traded currency pair, and it sets the import cost of energy and commodities for the twenty countries that use the euro.
fx-eur.recent: Deutsche Bank Research lifted its expected European Central Bank peak to 2.75%, arguing that energy costs are pushing the bank into a December hike on top of September's, with second-round passage into wages and services pricing as the stated fear. Politics pulled the other way: Alternative for Germany took 44.5% in Saxony-Anhalt, and Russia ordered Germany's St. Petersburg consulate shut by 18 September.

fx-jpy.standing: The price of one US dollar in Japanese yen, the most traded currency pair in Asia. Japan imports nearly all its energy in dollars, so a weaker yen raises the cost of everything the country burns.
fx-jpy.recent: Bessent pressed the Bank of Japan to raise rates, breaking the convention that a US Treasury Secretary leaves another central bank's decisions alone. The pressure landed on a currency already past 160, where the Ministry of Finance has intervened before, and traders bought yen back on the expectation Tokyo would tighten into the rate gap rather than defend the level with reserves.

fx-rub.standing: The exchange rate between Russia's ruble and the US dollar, quoted as rubles per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker ruble. Sanctions, oil export earnings and the central bank's key rate set where it trades.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble weakened alongside a fortnight of diplomatic and physical pressure on export earnings: a Ukrainian strike set an oil depot ablaze near Sochi, over 1,000km from the front, and Russia ordered Germany's St. Petersburg consulate shut by 18 September over the Leipzig drone dispute. Households moved 4.2 trillion rubles into cash.

fx-zar.standing: The price of one US dollar in South African rand, the most heavily traded currency in Africa and a standard proxy for emerging-market risk appetite. Commodity prices and domestic politics both move it, and import costs follow.
fx-zar.recent: The currency's firmer level did not reach the pump: the fuel formula carries a war-risk premium and a lag that held petrol up R1.34 a litre from Tuesday. Domestic politics gave little support — Dlomo's diversion of 12 million rand into covert operations, Gauteng nurses issuing the province a one-month ultimatum over austerity, and R88.6bn Treasury has identified sitting unclaimed in dormant accounts and pensions.

btc.standing: The price of one bitcoin in US dollars, the first and largest cryptocurrency, traded around the clock across exchanges worldwide with no central issuer or closing bell. It is the asset the rest of the crypto market is priced against.
btc.recent: A run above $80,000 came from short covering rather than fresh leverage, and the money went to basis traders arbitraging CME futures against spot rather than to directional buyers. BlackRock cut its in-kind swap threshold from $25 million to $1 million, and a bug in Blockstream's Elements software moved roughly 4,000 bitcoin out of the Liquid sidechain's federated reserve.

eth.standing: The native token of the Ethereum network, the largest smart-contract platform, where it pays the fees that execute code and settle transactions. Most stablecoins, lending protocols and tokenised assets are issued on top of it.
eth.recent: The rise ran with a broad crypto advance that carried bitcoin to $80,000 for the first time since May and pushed even Dogecoin and SHIB up as much as 100%, with ETF demand holding through the run. Monad's developers used the moment to propose quantum-safe wallets, an upgrade Ethereum is now weighing alongside bitcoin.

paxg.standing: A token redeemable for a fine troy ounce of London Good Delivery bullion held in vaults, so it trades on the metal's price while settling on a blockchain. It gives crypto holders a claim on gold without a custody account.
paxg.recent: A stronger-than-expected US payroll print lifted bets on a September Fed hike, pulling gold back late in the window, with a Jackson Hole speech by Warsh before it framing the rally as a wager on Fed independence. Underneath, the Dutch central bank moved $11.6bn of bullion out of New York to London, and the US Treasury sanctioned Turkey's Golden Global Bank over Iran-linked flows.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on artificial intelligence — the encyclopedia's general explainer on machines performing tasks associated with human reasoning. It is a rough gauge of how far a technology story has spread past the people already following it.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Nvidia agreed to pay $12.9 billion for Hugging Face, the neutral repository where open models had been hosted independently of any chip vendor, making each of its founders worth $1.8 billion. OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra to developers days later, and four large AI services went down the same Thursday morning on shared infrastructure.

wiki-russia.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Russia — the largest country on earth by land area, a nuclear-armed permanent member of the UN Security Council, and a top exporter of oil, gas, grain and uranium.
wiki-russia.recent: US envoys Witkoff and Kushner met Putin for three hours, and Kyiv ordered a battlefield halt for Sept. 5-8 to let them travel; the Kremlin has not ruled out a three-way format. Separately Moscow ordered Germany's St. Petersburg consulate shut by 18 September and closed three Goethe-Institut centres, retaliation for the Leipzig drone accusation.

wiki-pakistan.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Pakistan, a country of roughly 250 million people with a nuclear arsenal, a disputed border with India and another with Afghanistan. Traffic tracks what draws outside eyes to it.
wiki-pakistan.recent: A nursery fire at Islamabad's PIMS hospital killed fourteen infants, and reporting afterwards found the engineering posts responsible for the building's safety systems had been left vacant. Separately, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey convened the first committee meeting of the Mecca joint defence agreement in Istanbul.

wiki-china.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on China, the world's most populous state after India and its largest manufacturing economy. Views climb whenever a story with a Chinese actor at its centre reaches a general audience.
wiki-china.recent: A glacial flood tore through a border trade complex on the Tibetan side of the Nepal frontier on August 26, killing at least 95 in Nepal and leaving thousands missing; Beijing has published no list of its own dead, so families are identifying them in online posts. Customs then reported August exports of $401 billion, up 25% despite the tariff regime built to suppress them.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: The 33-kilometre-wide sea passage between Iran and Oman that links the Gulf to the Arabian Sea, and the only route out for crude loaded in Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Kuwait, Qatar and the UAE. Asia's refiners buy through it.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Six months into a war neither Washington nor Tehran has declared, US drones struck Iranian crude tankers and Iran answered with strikes on US airbases in Jordan and a vow to declare a prohibited zone in the strait. Merchant crews carry the cost: two Filipino sailors died aboard the Saudi-flagged Sidr, and India's crude basket reached $101.07 a barrel.

wiki-india.standing: Daily pageviews of the English Wikipedia article on India — a rough measure of how many people went looking for background on the country, and one that rises whenever something happening there reaches an audience outside it.
wiki-india.recent: Authorities demolished a mosque at dawn in Saharanpur on 5 September. The days around it carried a run of national stories: India fell to 6th-largest economy despite 7.8% growth, its crude basket hit $101.07 a barrel, and Adani Defence won a 5-year AK-203 ammunition deal.

wiki-ukraine.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Ukraine. It rises when the war forces itself onto front pages, so the count works as a rough gauge of how much of the world is paying attention at any given moment.
wiki-ukraine.recent: US envoys Witkoff and Kushner met Putin for three hours in Moscow and the Kremlin has not ruled out a three-way format, with Kyiv ordering a battlefield halt for Sept. 5-8 to accommodate the visit. Around it the war widened: Germany formally blamed Russia for a drone plot at Leipzig airport, and Ukrainian sea drones struck a vessel and an oil depot at Sochi.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Six months of US-Iran war have reached the shipping lane: Iran says it struck six tankers after US forces hit three, a supertanker was stopped after hitting mines, and Iran's security chief vowed to declare a prohibited zone in the strait. Two Filipino sailors died aboard the Saudi-flagged Sidr. Three tankers turned back without a shot fired.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Yemen's war restarted in full, with Houthi forces pressing an offensive toward the strait itself: 81 people were killed in a day of advances near Mokha, government forces counterattacked in the Taiz hills at a cost of over 120 lives since Thursday, and a strike on a prison at Al-Hazm killed 7. Somali pirates have hijacked 8 ships since April, adding a second hazard to the same approaches.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Traffic has recovered from the June trough as the Red Sea approach quieted, but the southern gate is contested again: Houthi advances near Mokha killed 81 in a day, and a strike on a prison in Al-Hazm killed 7, putting fighting back on the Bab al-Mandab that every Suez-bound hull must pass. Egypt spent the same fortnight hosting Xi Jinping and courting a Libya settlement.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Iran and the United States traded strikes on tankers at Hormuz, the gate the crude that later transits here must first clear, and Anak Krakatau's ash closed airspace over Jakarta rather than any sea lane. Neither reached this strait, and nothing else in the fortnight's reporting accounts for its traffic.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: China's customs administration reported a record August export month despite port disruption from extreme weather, with containers redirected toward Southeast Asia, Africa, the Gulf and Latin America as US tariffs bit. Taipei accused Beijing of espionage on the floor of a Pacific forum, and a US trade group pressed for a ban on Chinese-built cars.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: Gatun Lake is falling again under El Niño, and administrator Ilya Espino de Marotta says daily transits already trimmed from about 36 to 32 may drop to 29. The lake also supplies drinking water to roughly half of Panama's population, so rationing slots is the cheaper of two cuts. When slots are auctioned, grain and bulk carriers lose them first while container lines pay the fee.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Two collisions off Istanbul inside four days sank a Turkish cargo ship and left 10 crew missing, tightening pilotage and traffic separation through the channel just as grain movement drew scrutiny — the UN food agency's price index climbed a third month to 133.3 points. Turkey also summoned Kyiv's ambassador over strikes on Turkish-linked ships in the Black Sea.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: The pressure here sits at the edges rather than on the water. More than 72,000 people crossed into Ceuta in July and Morocco deported over 4,000 from Tangier in 20 days; Italy and Spain extended border checks to September 15. Hormuz's closure after two tanker attacks diverts Gulf crude away from the Mediterranean altogether.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Masked protesters blocked the roads into Dover on 5 September, shutting Britain's busiest ferry port and the cross-Channel freight running through it; the council leader said police were slow to respond. Two days later a crowd in Portsmouth blocked buses carrying 140 asylum seekers who had crossed from Normandy.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: US drones struck Iranian crude tankers near Kharg Island, and Iran says it hit six vessels in reply. Three more turned back in Hormuz after an IRGC warning, and Iran's security chief vowed a prohibited zone there. Owners are now pricing war risk into both of the Gulf's exits at once.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.

mkt:tadawul.standing: Saudi Arabia's main stock index, tracking the roughly 240 companies listed on the Saudi Exchange in Riyadh. It is the Arab world's largest market by value, dominated by Aramco, and trades Sunday to Thursday, opening the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: OPEC+ left its production quotas unchanged with Brent near $96, holding the oil revenue the index's largest constituents are priced against. Washington's separate nuclear agreement lets Saudi Arabia enrich uranium to 20% and skips the additional protocol, while Riyadh's new defence pact with Pakistan and Turkey held its first committee meeting in Istanbul.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest and most traded companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. Priced in lira, so its level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The US Treasury sanctioned Golden Global Bank over Iran-linked dealings, putting a listed Istanbul lender inside a compliance perimeter its peers have to price. Around it, Ankara summoned Kyiv's ambassador over strikes on Turkish ships in the Black Sea, and Erdogan cast his SCO push as a "360-degree" foreign policy rather than a break with the West.

mkt:dfm.standing: The main index of the Dubai Financial Market, tracking companies listed on the emirate's exchange. It is the Gulf's principal listing venue for property developers and banks, and moved to a Monday–Friday trading week in 2022, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: Fighting between the US and Iran has moved onto the Emirates' own waters: US forces hit three Iranian oil tankers, and the UAE downed an Iranian drone offshore. Washington is also pressing the banking side, with Bessent targeting UAE banks over Iran ties, and Hormuz disruption has cut hotel demand to a fraction of normal.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The 30 largest companies by value on Bursa Malaysia, the Kuala Lumpur exchange. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: Prosecutors charged former prime minister Ismail Sabri with concealing some $40 million in assets, the third Malaysian premier to face court. Malaysia's king then declared a smoke emergency in Sarawak as peat fires in Indonesia pushed haze across the border, and a promised repeal of the Peaceful Assembly Act's criminal penalties slipped again.

mkt:idx.standing: Indonesia's benchmark index, tracking every listed company on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta. Commodity producers and the big state and private banks carry most of its weight, so it moves with coal, nickel and domestic credit.
mkt:idx.recent: Prabowo has pulled the economy under his own imprint through the cooperatives push, and Jakarta has turned that reach outward: parliament ratified the Russian bloc deal and opened 138 oil and gas exploration blocks to Russian partners, with fertilizer and shipbuilding investment attached. Nickel smelting at Morowali keeps running on captive coal outside the national grid's accounting.

mkt:tse.standing: The oldest and most-watched index of Japanese shares, a price-weighted average of 225 large companies listed in Tokyo. Asia's largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: Treasury Secretary Bessent pressed the Bank of Japan to raise rates, and the yen then fell past 160 per dollar — a level that lifts the overseas earnings of Tokyo's exporters while raising the cost of the energy Japan imports. Fed hike odds moved to two-in-three as an oil shock reset the rate outlook.

mkt:hkex.standing: Hong Kong's benchmark index, tracking the largest companies listed in the territory, most of them mainland Chinese groups. It is where Chinese firms meet foreign capital, so it doubles as a daily read on outside sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: Regulators handed five state insurers and three banks $53.6 billion in fresh capital, which loosens the solvency charge that keeps insurers out of equities and points a large pool of long-duration savings toward listed shares. August customs figures then landed above forecast, with exports up 25% to $401 billion despite tariffs and storm-hit ports.

mkt:sse.standing: The main board in Shanghai, tracking every A-share and B-share listed there and dominated by state-owned banks, energy and industrial groups. Largely closed to foreign money, so domestic policy moves it more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: Regulators handed five state insurers and three banks $53.6 billion, a solvency injection that lowers the capital charge holding those funds out of equities and so widens who can buy Shanghai stock without the state buying a share itself. Customs then reported August exports up 25% to $401 billion, holding through the tariff regime built to suppress them.

mkt:krx.standing: The main index of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, weighted across every common stock listed on its senior board. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix dominate it, which makes it a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The Bank of Korea raised its policy rate to 3.00% in a second consecutive move, prioritising financial stability over growth, while SK Hynix said it was weighing closer ties with Kioxia. Seoul also spent the window denying it was readying a naval deployment to the Strait of Hormuz, the route its imported energy travels.

mkt:bse.standing: India's headline equity index, tracking 30 large companies traded on the BSE in Mumbai. The exchange opened in 1875, making it Asia's oldest, and the index is the reference point for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: India's crude basket crossed $101 a barrel on Friday, a direct cost for an economy that imports most of its oil, and rupee weakness pushed the country to sixth-largest economy by nominal dollar GDP even as output grew 7.8%. Defence localisation ran the other way, with Adani Defence taking a five-year AK-203 ammunition contract.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest and most traded companies listed on the Singapore Exchange, the city-state's main market. It leans heavily on the three domestic banks and on landlords with property across the region, so it reads as a gauge of Asian credit and rents.
mkt:sgx.recent: Trade running through Singapore held up better than the tariff regime implied: China reported August exports of $401 billion, a 25% rise, on a redirected destination mix. The city's own financial trade thinned in one corner, with $680 million of crypto funding going to only 25 deals.

mkt:twse.standing: Taiwan's benchmark index, tracking every listed common share on the Taiwan Stock Exchange in Taipei by market value. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: Nvidia paid $3.5 billion for convertible bonds giving it an option on MediaTek, whose shares jumped and pulled the wider index with them. Taipei separately accused Beijing of espionage on the floor of the Pacific forum, and prosecutors widened a hunt for engineers recruited into undeclared Chinese chip labs.

mkt:set.standing: The main index of the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, covering the listed companies that meet its size and liquidity tests. Tourism flows and regional energy prices move it more than most markets in Asia.
mkt:set.recent: Thailand's push to move up the semiconductor chain runs through Washington: a handful of firms control the fabrication equipment any new plant would need, and export controls decide who gets it. That leaves the exchange's industrial names dependent on American licensing rather than domestic policy.

mkt:pse.standing: The Philippine Stock Exchange Index tracks 30 of the largest and most actively traded companies listed in Manila. It is a small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: Two arrest warrants hit the political establishment in a week: an anti-graft court ordered the arrest of Marcos's cousin Romualdez over flood-control kickbacks, and a separate court ordered Vice President Sara Duterte arrested over alleged threats against Marcos, with bail set at $1,900 per charge.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed in Sydney by float-adjusted market value, the headline gauge for Australian shares. Mining and banking dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: Domestic rate pressure sits under the market: home prices fell for a fifth straight month while borrowing costs stayed where they are, and lenders moved toward a rate war as buyer numbers collapsed. Miners and energy names led the drag, and Canberra weighed a subsidy to keep an aluminium smelter open rather than let it close.

mkt:jse.standing: The FTSE/JSE All Share tracks nearly every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, Africa's largest market by capitalisation, weighted so that a handful of dual-listed miners and global holding companies carry much of the index.
mkt:jse.recent: The rally sat alongside a fiscal squeeze visible everywhere but the tape: Gauteng's nurses gave the province a month over austerity-driven staffing, and Treasury turned to R88.6bn of unclaimed money in dormant accounts and pensions as a revenue source. Petrol rose R1.34 a litre even as the rand strengthened, the fuel formula passing on a war premium.

mkt:b3.standing: The main index of B3 in São Paulo, tracking the most heavily traded shares on Brazil's only stock exchange. Iron ore, oil and the country's own interest rates drive it, making it Latin America's largest equity market.
mkt:b3.recent: The collapse of Bank Master in a fraud probe exposed a supervisory failure in Brasília, and a new poll on 2 September showed the socialist president's lead evaporating — a shift toward a market-friendlier succession that Brazilian equities have historically rewarded.

mkt:bmv.standing: Mexico's main equity index, tracking a weighted sample of the largest and most traded companies listed on the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City. It is tightly coupled to US demand and to the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The binding constraint on the cross-border economy this fortnight was water, not tariffs: the 1944 treaty obliges Mexico to deliver a fixed volume from the Rio Grande basin each five-year cycle, and a decade of drought means the volume does not exist. Washington can attach that debt to trade leverage, and the shortfall is settled out of Chihuahua and Tamaulipas farmers.

mkt:byma.standing: The main share index of the Buenos Aires exchange, tracking Argentina's largest listed companies. Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years; the direction over a day means something, the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: Milei reopened the Falklands claim against the UK and moved to sanction 45 firms and individuals tied to oil drilling around the islands. Trump then said the long-standing US position on the Falklands was one of many under review, putting Buenos Aires' most important foreign backer in play alongside its dispute with London.

mkt:tsx.standing: Canada's headline equity index, tracking the largest companies listed in Toronto by market value. Energy, mining and the big banks dominate its weighting, so it tends to trade on commodity prices more than on domestic growth.
mkt:tsx.recent: The index climbed through a summer in which Ottawa answered Washington's tariffs with a matching list taxing perfume, golf clubs and video consoles, and Ontario's Ford backed retaliation. The escalation turned personal in September, when Trump threatened by name to bar sales of Bombardier jets in the US market.

mkt:nyse.standing: The 500 largest US-listed companies weighted by market value, the benchmark most American retirement savings is measured against. Its close sets the tone every other market opens against.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies by market value listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: Argentina sanctioned 45 firms and individuals over UK-linked oil drilling off the Falklands, and Milei threatened further measures while Washington said its position on the islands was under review. None of that has landed as a UK market event, and nothing else in the fortnight accounts for the index.

mkt:xetra.standing: The 40 largest listed companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. Carmakers, chemicals and industrial engineering dominate it, so the index tracks the health of Europe's biggest export economy.
mkt:xetra.recent: Volkswagen dominated the corporate news: it will cut 50,000 more jobs worldwide, and its Osnabrück plant is being converted to weapons production under a deal with Aurelius that preserves 1,200 jobs. Deutsche Bank raised its expected ECB peak rate to 2.75% on second-round energy effects, and Alternative for Germany took 44.5% in Saxony-Anhalt.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest listed companies in France, traded on Euronext Paris. Luxury goods and energy dominate it, leaving the index unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: Two French export lines drew state money in the window: Sweden ordered four frigates from Naval Group at €1.1 billion each, and the European Space Agency split €544 million between three rocket startups, passing over Ariane's own MaiaSpace on an award now only "expected to resume." Against that, France's maize harvest fell to a four-decade low.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The blue-chip index of the 25 largest listed companies on the Amsterdam exchange, the world's oldest, founded in 1602. Chipmaking equipment is its heaviest weight, so a single supplier's order book moves the whole benchmark.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: Two Amsterdam stories set the backdrop: European gas passed €75 per megawatt-hour with EU storage at a record low heading into winter, a cost that lands on the index's chemical and industrial names, and the Dutch central bank moved $11.6bn in gold out of New York to London, a custody shift rather than a market one.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main exchange. Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make this a proxy for both regions.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 most liquid companies on the Milan exchange, Italy's main equity market. Banks and utilities carry it, and it is the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: Giorgia Meloni passed 1,413 days in office to become Italy's longest-serving prime minister, the tenure that has held Italian debt spreads down for the banks that dominate the index. Former leaders told CNBC economic reform must now follow. Rome also renewed its Schengen suspension with Spain, extending border checks to September 15.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index: the 20 largest and most traded companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry the index, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The 30 most traded companies on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms dominate it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: Stockholm signed a €4.3 billion deal for four French frigates from Naval Group, each costing €1.1 billion — an order that goes to a French yard rather than a Swedish one, and lands as four EU countries push to reopen the debate on using frozen Russian assets for Ukraine.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only public equity market. It trades Sunday to Thursday, and banks, defence contractors and technology firms carry most of its weight.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at the next meeting. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves whenever incoming data shifts the balance between a hold, a cut and a hike.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia biography of the 45th and 47th president of the United States. It is one of the most-read political pages on the site, and its traffic rises whenever a decision out of Washington lands abroad.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: The Sept. 3 peak came as US strikes on Iran resumed and 11 people were killed, a war Trump called "small potatoes" while Vance declined to name it a war at all; the Mint put his face on a $1 coin the same day. Witkoff and Kushner then met Putin for three hours in Moscow, and Kyiv ordered a battlefield halt for the visit.

wiki-united-states.standing: The daily count of people opening the English Wikipedia article on the United States. It is a rough gauge of how much of the world is turning to look at the country at any given moment, and it rises when Washington acts abroad.
wiki-united-states.recent: The late-August rise came as US forces struck Iran for the first time in a month, then hit new targets as hostilities flared and eleven were killed. Washington followed with strikes on three Iranian crude tankers, and Iran's security chief vowed a prohibited zone in the Strait of Hormuz, where two Filipino sailors died aboard the tanker Sidr.

wiki-nepal.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Nepal, the Himalayan republic between India and China. Counts rise when the country enters world news and fall back within days, so the series tracks foreign attention rather than anything domestic.
wiki-nepal.recent: A glacial lake outburst on August 26 — ice and rock collapsing rather than rain — sent a flood down the Trishuli toward the Chinese border, killing more than a thousand and trapping 934 workers at hydropower sites in Rasuwa. Two men were pulled alive from the Chilime tunnel after nine days. The border trade corridor to China closed again.

fed-funds.standing: The overnight rate the Federal Reserve sets for banks lending reserves to each other. It is the anchor for dollar borrowing costs everywhere, and mortgage, corporate and emerging-market debt pricing follows from it.
fed-funds.recent: Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole debut repriced the dollar, and markets swung from expecting easing to favoring a September hike. A payroll surge and an oil shock pushed hike odds to two-in-three, while the long end sold off on term premium rather than policy: the 10-year Treasury reached 4.81% and the 30-year mortgage rate 6.71%.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on cash parked with it overnight. It is the floor under euro-area borrowing costs, so mortgages, business loans and the euro itself reprice off it.
ecb-rate.recent: Deutsche Bank raised its expected peak to 2.75%, arguing energy costs are feeding into wages and services pricing rather than staying in the barrel. The ECB cannot produce oil, so holding rates high means squeezing the rest of the basket to absorb a supply shock — and borrowers priced off the euro curve in Cairo, Rabat and Ankara pay for it too.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force that is out of work and actively looking, published monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. It is the figure the Federal Reserve weighs against inflation when setting interest rates.
us-unemployment.recent: A solid US jobs report on 5 September pushed Treasury yields and the dollar up and knocked equities back, the reaction of a market that reads a firm labour market as one less reason for the Federal Reserve to cut.

wiki-nigeria.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Nigeria, Africa's most populous country and its largest oil producer. The count rises when a political, security or economic story sends people looking for background on the country.
wiki-nigeria.recent: Uber shut down in Nigeria and Uganda with immediate effect on 2 September, leaving drivers and passengers with no notice or wind-down for contractors. Dangote Cement booked a London investor day rather than raise at home, and the House of Representatives dissolved ad hoc oversight committees, not one of which had ever filed a report.

xag.standing: A digital token backed one-for-one by an ounce of allocated physical silver held in audited vaults, quoted in dollars per ounce. It tracks the silver market but trades on its own venue, so its price can part from spot.
xag.recent: Nothing in the past fortnight accounts for a move of this size. The nearest touchpoints are industrial: China's installed solar capacity reached 1,286 gigawatts by July, and Pakistan's regulator attached a battery requirement to an 800MW solar and wind auction. Neither is large enough to reprice the metal.

wiki-petroleum.standing: The English Wikipedia article on petroleum — crude oil, the liquid hydrocarbon that refineries split into fuels, lubricants and the feedstock for most plastics. Daily readership of it rises when supply is disrupted or fuel prices bite.
wiki-petroleum.recent: The two tankers attacked leaving Hormuz on 2 September, and the closure that followed, put crude at the centre of a widening war; US strikes on three Iranian tankers came days later, and 2 Filipino sailors died aboard the Sidr. American pump prices reached $4.03 a gallon, above the 2012 record, while Washington took a stake in Venezuela's reserves.

poly-israel-closes-its-airspace-by-septe.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Israel shuts its civil airspace to commercial flights before a set date. Airspace closure is the clearest market-visible sign that a regional exchange of fire has begun, so carriers and insurers watch it as a war tripwire.
poly-israel-closes-its-airspace-by-septe.recent: The contract went from near-nothing to near-certain over ten days as the fighting widened past Gaza: Israeli strikes destroyed Ghandour Hospital in Nabatieh in southern Lebanon, killing seven, and Netanyahu said in Gaza that "we are not retreating." The escalation drew legal pressure too, with the UN's Volker Turk telling states to halt arms transfers over the risk of complicity.

poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that settles at full value if Lula wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election, priced in cents on the dollar. It is what traders will pay on the leadership of Latin America's largest economy, not a poll.

us-cpi.standing: The year-over-year change in the US Consumer Price Index, published monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. It sets the reference rate for Social Security adjustments and wage bargaining, and the Federal Reserve's rate path answers to it.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: The count of oil tankers passing each day through the Strait of Hormuz, the sea lane between Iran and Oman that carries roughly a fifth of the world's traded crude. Nothing that ships out of the Gulf reaches a refinery without crossing it.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: Six months of war between the US and Iran reached the shipping lane itself: the US struck three Iranian crude tankers and Iran said it hit six in reply, a supertanker was stopped by mines in the strait, and Iran's security chief vowed a new prohibited zone. Two Filipino sailors died aboard the Saudi-flagged Sidr. India's crude basket passed $101 a barrel.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: Daily count of container ships transiting the strait between Yemen and Djibouti, the southern gate to the Red Sea and the Suez route. Almost every Asia–Europe box ship passes here, or else adds two weeks going round the Cape.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: Fighting has come back to the Yemeni coast: the Houthis pushed toward the strait from Mokha in advances that killed 81 people in a single day, Yemen's army answered with air strikes over the Taiz hills, and more than 120 people were killed from Thursday onward. Somali pirates have taken 8 ships since April, closing the alternative route south.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The number of vessels passing through Egypt's Suez Canal each day, the sea-level link between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea. Roughly a tenth of world trade moves through it, and what deters ships at the Bab al-Mandab shows up here.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: The canal's southern approach ran through a fighting season: Houthi forces advanced on the strait around Mokha in a day that killed 81, Yemen's army struck back over Taiz, and Somali pirates have hijacked eight ships since April, pushing lines back onto the Cape route. Xi Jinping's Cairo visit pressed Egypt on a security order it cannot enforce at sea.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: Daily count of vessels crossing Panama's lock system between the Atlantic and Pacific, a route carrying a large share of US east-coast container and grain trade. Each crossing drains fresh water from a lake reservoir, so capacity depends on rainfall.
portwatch-panama-total.recent: Administrator Ilya Espino de Marotta is weighing a further cut in daily transits to 29 from 32 as Gatun Lake falls, a reservoir that also supplies drinking water to about half of Panama's population. The squeeze is El Niño: the WMO puts the odds near 100% that it persists into February. Rationed slots get auctioned, pricing out grain and bulk carriers first.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The count of ships passing daily through the narrow sea lane between Sumatra and the Malay Peninsula, the shortest route between the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea. Most of East Asia's imported oil and much of its container trade rides through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: The strait carries the traffic Hormuz is shedding: three tankers turned back at the Gulf entrance, US strikes hit three Iranian crude tankers, and Iran's security chief vowed a new prohibited zone, pushing war-risk cost onto every Gulf-to-Asia voyage. China reported exports up 25% to $401 billion, and India's crude basket reached $101.07 a barrel — both cargoes that transit here.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: The daily count of merchant vessels passing through the channel between Taiwan and mainland China, one of the busiest lanes in world trade. Container and LNG cargoes from Northeast Asia to Europe and the Gulf run through it.
portwatch-taiwan-total.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's shipping news concerns this channel. The disruption sits at Hormuz instead, where three tankers turned back, two Filipino sailors died aboard the Sidr, and Iran's security chief vowed a prohibited zone. None of it bears on traffic here.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The count of ships passing daily through the Dover Strait, the narrow neck of water between England and France that funnels traffic between the North Sea and the Channel. It is one of the busiest shipping lanes anywhere, and cross-Channel ferries thread through it alongside the through traffic.
portwatch-dover-total.recent: Masked anti-migrant protesters shut Britain's busiest ferry port at Dover on 5 September, halting cross-Channel freight, and a council leader said police were slow to respond. Two days later crowds blocked buses carrying 140 asylum seekers who had landed at Portsmouth after crossing from Normandy.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through the Strait of Gibraltar, the nine-mile gap between Spain and Morocco that is the Mediterranean's only Atlantic door. Everything sailing between the two seas is counted here.
portwatch-gibraltar-total.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's reporting accounts for the traffic. What it does carry from the strait's own shores is the Ceuta migrant crisis — Spain questioning Morocco's border control, and over 4,000 people seeking to cross deported from Tangier in 20 days — a movement of people across the water rather than of shipping along it.

poly-will-marine-le-pen-win-the-2027-fre.standing: A Polymarket contract that settles at one dollar if Marine Le Pen becomes president of France in the 2027 election, and at nothing otherwise. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, quoted as a percentage.
poly-will-marine-le-pen-win-the-2027-fre.recent: The fortnight's coverage concerned the venues rather than this contract: New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to rule on prediction markets, the Ninth Circuit held that sports bets are not "swaps", and a White House aide paid $170,000 to end an insider-trading probe over betting on speeches. None of it bears on the French race.

poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Vladimir Putin ceases to be Russia's president before the end of 2026, whether by resignation, removal, death or a lost election. Traders price it as a running read on the durability of one man's grip on the Russian state.
poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.recent: The window covered a stretch in which Putin remained the fixed point of every channel around the war: Witkoff and Kushner met him in Moscow for three hours, Modi pressed him on Ukraine at the Shanghai bloc summit in Bishkek, and Ukraine ordered a battlefield halt to accommodate the envoys. Nothing in that fortnight touched the succession question the contract is written on.

poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-repub.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Marco Rubio becomes the Republican nominee for president in 2028. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves years before any primary votes are cast.
poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-repub.recent: The fortnight's news about this venue concerned the venue itself rather than the field: the Ninth Circuit held that sports bets on Kalshi are not "swaps," confirming state power over prediction markets, Connecticut filed suit, and New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to settle preemption. A White House aide was also fined for betting on speeches he read early. None of it bears on Rubio's standing.

poly-will-gavin-newsom-win-the-2028-us-p.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Gavin Newsom, the governor of California, becomes US president in the 2028 election. It trades as a cents-on-the-dollar price, so a share paying $1 if he wins tells you what buyers will risk on that outcome.
poly-will-gavin-newsom-win-the-2028-us-p.recent: The venues carrying contracts like this spent the window fighting over whether they may exist. The Ninth Circuit ruled in San Francisco that Kalshi's sports contracts are not "swaps" and so fall under state gambling power, New Jersey then asked the Supreme Court to settle federal preemption, and a White House aide who read speeches early paid $170,000 to close an insider-trading probe.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Israel and Iran hold to a truce by a set date. Traders price it as a wager on whether the exchanges of fire stop, and it moves on strikes, mediation and the shipping lanes the fighting reaches.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: US strikes resumed on 30 August and intensified through the first week of September, with 11 killed and Iran promising a 'more painful response'; the UAE intercepted a drone. CENTCOM video showed three Iranian crude tankers struck, Iran's security chief vowed a prohibited zone at Hormuz, and two sailors died aboard the tanker Sidr.

poly-will-openai-have-the-best-ai-model-.standing: A Polymarket contract that settles on whether OpenAI holds the top-ranked AI model at a fixed date. Quoted as a percentage, the price is simply what traders will pay for that outcome, and it shifts whenever a rival lab ships.
poly-will-openai-have-the-best-ai-model-.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's reporting bears on which lab leads. What news there was concerned the venues themselves: New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to settle who regulates prediction markets, and the Ninth Circuit ruled that Kalshi's sports contracts are not swaps, leaving states a hand in licensing them.

poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether United Russia, the party that has held a supermajority in the State Duma since its founding, wins the most seats at the next legislative election. Traders price a party that controls the ballot it runs on.
poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.recent: Russia's war footing framed the fortnight: Witkoff and Kushner met Putin for three hours in Moscow, Ukraine ordered a battlefield halt for the visit, and Germany formally blamed Moscow for a drone plot at Leipzig while the Kremlin summoned Berlin's chargé d'affaires and moved to close Goethe-Institut centres. None of it touches the party's grip on the Duma.

poly-us-iran-final-nuclear-deal-by-decem.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Washington and Tehran sign a nuclear agreement before the end of 2026. It prices how much traders will pay for diplomacy to survive, and it moves against every escalation in the Gulf.
poly-us-iran-final-nuclear-deal-by-decem.recent: US forces struck three Iranian crude tankers and Iran said it hit six in reply, and Iran's security chief vowed a prohibited zone in the Strait of Hormuz. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said he doubts a deal is coming. Two Filipino sailors died aboard the tanker Sidr as crews were caught in the stalemate.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if the United States lifts its naval blockade of Iran before the end of 2026. Traders price it as a running read on whether Washington's maritime pressure campaign is closer to being wound down or entrenched.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Strikes resumed after a month's pause and then widened: CENTCOM hit three Iranian crude tankers, Iran said it struck six in reply, and Tehran's security chief vowed a new prohibited zone in the Strait of Hormuz. Energy Secretary Chris Wright then said there may be no nuclear agreement at all — the aim the campaign was declared to serve.

poly-will-nvidia-be-the-largest-company-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if NVIDIA has the largest market capitalisation of any listed company on its resolution date. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with the race at the top of the US market.
poly-will-nvidia-be-the-largest-company-.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's reporting bears on NVIDIA's market value; what it carries is a fight over where these contracts may trade at all. The Ninth Circuit held that sports bets are not swaps, Connecticut sued Kalshi, and New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to settle who regulates the venues.

wiki-israel.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Israel. The count is a rough gauge of how many people outside a story's immediate region are looking up the country itself rather than following a specific event.
wiki-israel.recent: Volker Turk told states to stop transferring arms to Israel where they risk being used in violations, and told companies to end business supporting illegal settlements — an argument that puts third-state suppliers, not only the occupation, inside the legal frame. Israeli strikes destroyed Ghandour Hospital in Nabatieh, killing seven.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Democrats hold a majority in the US House after the 2026 midterms. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it shifts on redistricting rulings, retirements and primary results.
poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's reporting accounts for the price. What it carried was the Missouri Supreme Court blocking a Trump-backed map from November's midterms, and pressure on the venue itself: the Ninth Circuit ruled sports bets aren't "swaps," and New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to settle who polices these contracts.

poly-friedrich-merz-out-as-chancellor-of.standing: A Polymarket contract settling on whether Friedrich Merz holds the German chancellorship before 2027. Its price is what traders pay for that outcome in cents on the dollar, and it moves with coalition arithmetic in the Bundestag.

poly-will-magdalena-andersson-be-the-nex.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Magdalena Andersson, Sweden's Social Democrat leader and a former prime minister, takes the office next. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, quoted as a percentage.
poly-will-magdalena-andersson-be-the-nex.recent: Nothing in the past fortnight's material bears on this contract's outcome. What ran instead concerned the venues themselves: the Ninth Circuit upheld state power over Kalshi's sports contracts, New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to settle who regulates them, and a White House aide paid a fine for betting on speeches he read early.

poly-will-gadi-eizenkot-be-the-next-prim.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Gadi Eizenkot, the former Israeli army chief of staff who moved into opposition politics, forms the next government in Israel. Traders price it as a read on whether Netanyahu's coalition holds.
poly-will-gadi-eizenkot-be-the-next-prim.recent: Nothing in the past fortnight bears on who forms the next government. What came out of Israel was Smotrich's claim on Areas A and B, Ben-Gvir's first-year expulsion quota of 250,000, and strikes in Gaza and on Ghandour Hospital in Nabatieh — the conduct of the war, not the arithmetic of a coalition.

poly-will-no-fed-rate-cuts-happen-in-202.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate untouched across every scheduled meeting of the calendar year. It is a bet on the direction of American borrowing costs, and mortgage, corporate and emerging-market pricing all sit downstream of it.
poly-will-no-fed-rate-cuts-happen-in-202.recent: An oil shock pushed traders toward a hike rather than a cut, and a payroll surge on top of it lifted September hike odds enough to pressure gold. Kevin Warsh told Jackson Hole the Fed would have "work to do" if inflation did not fade, and bitcoin fell under $79,000 as traders positioned for tightening.

poly-will-gavin-newsom-win-the-2028-demo.standing: A Polymarket contract on which candidate the Democratic Party nominates for president in 2028, priced as the share traders will pay for a Gavin Newsom win. It is a bet on a party's internal choice, not a poll of voters.
poly-will-gavin-newsom-win-the-2028-demo.recent: The fortnight's news about this market was regulatory rather than political: the Ninth Circuit ruled that sports contracts are not "swaps" and confirmed state power over prediction markets, Connecticut added a suit against Kalshi, and New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to settle preemption. Separately, a White House aide paid a fine for betting on speeches he read early. None of it bears on the nomination itself.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency whose ledger hides sender, recipient and amount by default, unlike Bitcoin's public chain. That privacy makes it the settlement asset of choice for ransomware crews and for anyone moving value outside the banking system.
xmr.recent: Two strands of the fortnight's reporting run through this coin. A group calling itself VantaCore began hitting Russian companies with custom ransomware, the kind of campaign whose payments are demanded in an asset that cannot be traced; and North Korea has built out earnings that never pass through a bank.

wiki-germany.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Germany, the European Union's largest economy and most populous member state. The count climbs when the country's politics or its role in a wider conflict draws outside attention.
wiki-germany.recent: Alternative for Germany took 44.5% in Saxony-Anhalt, the first far-right win in a German state election since the Second World War, and still fell short of a governing majority as the other parties refused a coalition. In parallel, Berlin formally blamed Russia for a bomb-rigged drone near a cargo plane at Leipzig, and Moscow answered by ordering the St. Petersburg consulate shut by 18 September and closing three Goethe-Institut centres.

stocks:BBD.standing: The New York-listed shares of Brazil's largest private-sector bank, a retail and commercial lender with branches in every Brazilian municipality. Its earnings track household credit and the delinquency rate across the country.

poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether a specific piece of US crypto market-structure legislation, the Clarity Act, becomes law before the end of the calendar year. It is a bet on congressional floor time, not on the bill's merits.
poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.recent: The slide followed a bad fortnight for the prediction-market industry the bill would help legitimise: the Ninth Circuit ruled that Kalshi's sports contracts are not "swaps" and confirmed state power to regulate them, Connecticut filed a fresh suit, and New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to settle preemption. A White House teleprompter operator also paid a fine to close an insider-trading case over bets on the president's speeches.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if the United States lifts its naval blockade of Iranian shipping before the end of September 2026. Traders price it as a read on whether the maritime campaign in the Gulf winds down or hardens.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: The contract collapsed as the campaign widened rather than closed: US forces struck three Iranian crude tankers, Iran said it hit six in reply, and three tankers turned back at Hormuz without a shot fired. Tehran's security chief then vowed a prohibited zone across the Gulf, and Energy Secretary Chris Wright cast doubt on a nuclear deal.

poly-will-new-people-nl-gain-the-most-se.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the party New People wins the most seats in the election it names. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome — a running market read on who ends up controlling a legislature, not a poll.

stocks:2222.SR.standing: Saudi Arabia's state oil producer, listed on the Tadawul exchange with only a small fraction of its shares in public hands. It pumps more crude than any other company, and its dividend is a main source of the Saudi state budget.
stocks:2222.SR.recent: The only item in the fortnight's coverage touching the company is a Houthi strike on Saudi energy facilities at Jazan that wounded 73 civilians and halted production there, and it falls after this series ends, so nothing in the record accounts for the share price.

stocks:NVS.standing: One of the largest pharmaceutical companies in the world, headquartered in Basel, Switzerland, and listed in New York as an American depositary receipt. Its value rests on a pipeline of patented drugs, so late-stage trial results move it.
stocks:NVS.recent: Two late-stage Novartis readouts missed within days of each other. Pelacarsen, aimed at lowering lipoprotein(a), did not prevent heart attacks or strokes; del-desiran then failed to improve muscle function in myotonic dystrophy, the most common adult-onset muscular dystrophy and one with no approved disease-modifying treatment.

poly-will-china-invade-taiwan-before-202.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out only if Chinese forces invade Taiwan before the end of 2026. Its price, read as a percentage, is what traders will pay for that outcome — a live cost on the risk of war in the Pacific.
poly-will-china-invade-taiwan-before-202.recent: The fortnight's coverage of this venue is about who may run it, not about Taiwan: New Jersey took the regulatory fight to the Supreme Court, the Ninth Circuit backed state power over Kalshi, and a White House aide was fined for betting on speeches he had read early. None of it bears on this contract.

poly-will-douard-philippe-win-the-2027-f.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Édouard Philippe — French prime minister from 2017 to 2020, now mayor of Le Havre and leader of the Horizons party — wins the 2027 presidential election. The price is what traders pay for that outcome.
poly-will-douard-philippe-win-the-2027-f.recent: Nothing in the month's material touches the French race. What it carries instead concerns the venue: New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to rule on state power over prediction markets, the Ninth Circuit held that sports bets aren't swaps, and a White House aide was fined for betting on speeches he read early.

poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-republic.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if J.D. Vance becomes the Republican Party's nominee for president in 2028. It trades as a running price on the succession question inside the party rather than on any vote yet held.
poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-republic.recent: The window's news about this market was about the venue, not the candidate. The Ninth Circuit ruled in San Francisco that sports bets are not "swaps," confirming state power over prediction markets, Connecticut filed suit against Kalshi, and New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to settle who regulates the contracts. Separately a White House aide paid a fine for trading on speeches he read early.

stocks:NET.standing: Shares in the American network company that sits between visitors and much of the world's web, selling content delivery, DNS, DDoS protection and edge computing. When it fails, a slice of the internet fails with it.
stocks:NET.recent: The only reporting on the company in the window was a measurement, out of Amsterdam, of how much of the European web now terminates on its network — 9 in 10 sites. That is a question about concentration and sovereignty rather than about the business, and none of it accounts for the share price.

poly-2026-balance-of-power-r-senate-r-ho.standing: A Polymarket contract on Republicans holding both chambers after the 2026 midterms. It pays out only if the party keeps the Senate and the House together, so it prices a narrower outcome than either chamber's own market.
poly-2026-balance-of-power-r-senate-r-ho.recent: The fortnight's news about this market was about the venue rather than the vote: New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to decide whether federal swaps rules preempt state gambling law, the Ninth Circuit ruled that sports contracts on Kalshi are not swaps and left states their regulatory powers, and Connecticut filed suit on the same question. None of it bears on how a midterm sweep is priced.

poly-will-jean-luc-mlenchon-win-the-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Jean-Luc Mélenchon, founder of the left-wing La France Insoumise and a three-time presidential candidate, takes the 2027 French presidency. The price is what traders pay for that outcome, not a poll.

poly-kharg-island-no-longer-under-irania.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Iran loses control of Kharg Island before the end of the year. The island terminal handles the bulk of Iranian crude exports, so the price is a bet on whether the country's oil revenue survives the war intact.
poly-kharg-island-no-longer-under-irania.recent: The US struck three Iranian crude tankers, and Tehran answered on paper rather than at Kharg: Rezaei threatened a maritime exclusion zone across the Gulf and the security council vowed a prohibited zone at Hormuz, both of which raise insurance costs without contesting the terminal. Two Filipino sailors died aboard the tanker Sidr.
